SMTO-JOB-0012 — A background time limit was set on a normal command

GUID: 0479eb44-8757-439d-9fc9-38020332e027
Slug: job-lifetime-scope-invalid
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • The agent gave a command a time limit that only applies to background jobs, but the command wasn't set to run in the background. SMTO refused it before starting, so the command did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the agent continue; it normally resends the command without the background time limit. Removing the setting that doesn't apply is all this command needs to run.
  2. If it happens again, tell the agent whether you want the command to run in the background or to run normally while you wait for the result. The background time limit only works for background jobs, so the agent needs to know which one you want.
  3. If the command should stop after a certain time, say so plainly, for example "stop it if it takes longer than 10 minutes". The agent can then choose the right kind of limit for how the command runs.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and the task shows its result or a running background job.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same command unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • job_lifetime_seconds was supplied on an operation whose effective execution mode is not background, so the call was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • job_lifetime_seconds remains on an operation whose effective execution mode is not background. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • job_lifetime_seconds remains on an operation whose effective execution mode is not background.

How to diagnose it

  • Check effective background policy and normalization, not only the caller's requested flag.

How to fix it

  • Send job_lifetime_seconds only together with background=true on a call eligible for managed background execution; for other calls omit it and use timeout_seconds. When background execution is disabled by policy, an explicit background request already has its lifetime dropped automatically.
  • Use the lifetime field only for a deliberately selected background job. Omit it for foreground execution; model timeout controls do not govern this job lifetime.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Job lifetime applies only to an accepted background operation; foreground work uses its own timeout boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
